To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the 'naked', reduced subunits of mucus glycoprotein contain two kinds of protein antigenic determinants, one shared by the whole mucins, and the other 'cryptic', i.e. not exposed on the surface; (ii) both kinds of epitopes are also present in the 'heavily glycosylated' T-domains; (iii) the 'nude' protein domains are stabilized by disulphi...

polyclonal antibodies directed against the protein core of human cervical mucins react with epitopes that are shared by all human mucus glycopeptides, and that the protein core contains cryptic epitopes that are not accessible in the intact molecule.

(i) polyclonal antibodies raised in rabbits against reduced subunits of cervical mucus glyco proteins are directed towards both protein and carbohydrate determinants; (ii) the protein epitopes are 'naked' and are probably located within folded protein domains of the mucin molecule, whereas the carbohydrate epitopes are probably located at the surface; (iii) the protein determinants are shared by human bronchial, salivary, gastric and cervical mucus glycosylated proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of protein epitopes of human mucus.
the characterization of protein epitopes in the 'naked protein' domains of human muci
the characterization of a family of 'cryptic' epitopes within the protein domains of human mucins, which may be useful as markers in the study of the biosynthesis and secretion of these molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antibodies raised against reduced cervical mucin subunits recognize both the 'naked', exposed protein domains and the cryptic protein epitopes within the folded protein domains.

the antibodies are directed to protein structures, which are present in both the T- and the P-domains, and that these structures are shared by the 'naked', i.e. reduced subunits, and the 'naked protein domains' (T-domains).

the 'naked', i.e. reduced, domains of mucus glycoprotein subunits are composed of a common core protein with a variable number of carbohydrate side-chains, and that these domains share some protein epitopes with each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the protein core of mucus glycoprotein molecules is highly conserved and contains cryptic epitopes that are probably involved in the formation of a protective mucous layer.
human mucins have a core protein with a conserved primary structure and a conserved secondary structure.

human mucus glycopeptides contain a number of protein epitopes which are not accessible for antibodies, unless they are exposed by the action of reducing agents or proteases, and that the 'naked', exposed protein epitopes are shared by mucus glycoprotein molecules of different origin.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 'naked', i.e. reduced and unfolded protein domains of human mucins are antigenically similar, and that the protein domains in the native glycoprotein are folded in such a way that they are not recognized as antigens by the rabbit antibodies.
the 'naked protein domains' of human mucus are antigenic, and that they share common epitopes.
human mucins share epitopes within the protein domains.
